purpose: Run a Termux-owned Python/Linux processor loop that reads broker-owned status and stream-registry state, computes bounded diagnostic feedback, and publishes that feedback back to the broker while a foreground XR app remains active.
authority_boundary: Termux remains a normal Android app sidecar and processor module.
The broker remains the authority for stream identity, module state, provider ownership, and published-event acceptance.
The sidecar does not acquire headset sensors, own biometric device sessions, route high-rate media, or become a hidden watchdog.
Feedback is low-rate diagnostic or derived data, published through an explicit broker route such as diagnostics:termux_python.
preflight: Meta Quest workflow is active for live device operations.
A broker endpoint exposes bounded status and stream-registry state to the sidecar.
Termux can run Python or another reviewed Linux userland tool from its normal app sandbox.
The feedback stream id, poll interval, payload size, timeout, and stop condition are explicit before launch.
The foreground XR app does not depend on Termux for display, HOME behavior, or broker authority.
start: Start the broker and confirm its status endpoint is reachable from the sidecar route.
Start the Termux processor loop with a bounded poll interval and run duration.
Poll broker status and stream-registry state.
Compute a compact feedback payload from the broker-owned state.
Publish the feedback payload to the broker through the explicit feedback stream.
Foreground the XR app and keep the sidecar loop running for the planned stress window.
status: The broker accepts feedback events and reports them in its diagnostics or stream registry.
The foreground XR app remains active while sidecar feedback continues.
The sidecar records publish acknowledgements, latency, sequence number, and failure counts.
The feedback payload remains small, bounded, and derived from broker-visible state.
stop: Stop the Termux processor loop by recorded process id or service control.
Confirm no unexpected listener remains exposed.
Leave the broker and foreground app state to the owning workflow unless cleanup is explicitly part of the run.
cleanup: Keep real run logs, device paths, package identities, and timing dumps as local evidence only.
Promote only sanitized findings, synthetic examples, or schema changes to public docs.
Record whether failures were sidecar, broker-route, foreground-app, or cleanup issues.
evidence: Broker status snapshots before and after the sidecar run.
Stream-registry snapshots showing the feedback stream.
Feedback publish acknowledgements and latency summary.
Foreground XR app liveness or cadence evidence.
Sidecar process start, stop, and cleanup evidence.
risks: Short foreground tests do not prove survival across sleep, reboot, or battery restrictions.
A real product route needs authentication, payload limits, backpressure, cancellation, and audit logs.
A broker restart or stream-registry change can require reconnect behavior in the sidecar.
Do not use this low-rate control/diagnostic route for camera frames, audio, or other high-rate media.
